definition.title: Definition
definition.content: Socioeconomic Classification (CSE) is a measure of household welfare used by the Peruvian State in the Household Targeting System (SISFOH). It is obtained through an official procedure; UMBRAL does not calculate or certify your classification.

purpose.title: What is it for?
purpose.content: Some social programs and public interventions use CSE as one of their criteria. Having a CSE does not automatically enroll you or guarantee a benefit: each program checks its other requirements.
examples: Free SIS coverage and certain Pronabec scholarships
purpose.examplesTitle: Examples of interventions that use CSE

whoCanApply.title: Who can apply?
whoCanApply.content: An adult household member can submit the first application at the ULE of the district where the household currently lives. They do not have to own the dwelling or be the head of the family. This guide is for adults; ask the ULE about special situations.
requirements: Be an adult household member (18 or older)
Present household members’ identity documents: DNI, CE or CPP, as applicable; ask the ULE about other identification or temporarily missing documents
Bring an electricity bill no more than three months old, only if the dwelling has that service

important.title: Important
notes: UMBRAL prepares you for your first application; it does not process or decide CSE.
The ULE receives the application and collects information; the competent authorities determine the official classification.
The application is free and you do not need intermediaries.
Give clear, complete and truthful information to the authority. See sources and dates in Resources.

steps.title: Before you start
steps.content:
This guide prepares adults for a first CSE application. The procedure is free and takes place at the ULE of the municipality of the household’s current district of residence.

**What CSE is**

CSE is an official household classification. It does not automatically enroll you in social programs or guarantee benefits; each program checks its other criteria. UMBRAL does not apply for, calculate or certify CSE.

**Who can apply**

An adult household member (18 or older) can attend. They do not have to be the head of the family or own the dwelling. Ask the ULE for guidance on special situations.

**What household means**

People who share a dwelling and a budget for basic needs. This does not necessarily include everyone in the building or at the same address.

See official sources and their dates in Resources. You do not need to check every box before asking for guidance.

steps.title: Documents I need to gather
steps.content:
Review the identity documents of your household members. If you have a question, ask the ULE for guidance without waiting to complete every preparation item.

**Identity documents**

- DNI, Alien Registration Card (CE) or Temporary Stay Permit Card (CPP), as applicable, for all household members, including children.
- The directive also covers identification recognized by the competent authority. Ask the ULE if you have another document or someone is temporarily undocumented; this does not automatically exclude the whole household.

**Electricity bill, only if you have the service**

Bring an electricity bill for the dwelling that is no more than three months old. If the dwelling has no electricity service, that bill is not required.

**Additional documents**

The reviewed general list does not require a water bill, birth certificates, proof of address, a property title or income slips as additional documents for a first application. Copies are not listed as a general requirement.

If your DNI address differs from where you live, that alone does not require updating it before applying. Updating your address with Reniec is a recommendation; ask the ULE about other identification questions.

steps.title: Information they will request from me
steps.content:
Official information is declared to the ULE. UMBRAL does not ask you for names, document numbers, income or an address: here you only mark your preparation.

**About your household**

Review who shares the dwelling and the budget for basic needs. Staff can help you correctly register household members and their situation.

**About the dwelling and household economy**

Think about the current address and landmarks, the dwelling’s characteristics and services, and household members’ economic activities. Answer the official form’s questions with clear, complete and truthful information.

**If you do not remember something**

Ask staff for help and explain your question; do not invent answers. The ULE provides assistance with completing the application. You do not need a UMBRAL form or to attach personal documents here.

The Single Socioeconomic Form (FSU) is an official instrument. Its implementation may vary; this guide does not reproduce its form or the CSE calculation.

steps.title: Where and how to submit the application
steps.content:
Go to the Local Registration Unit (ULE) of the municipality of your current district of residence. Check your district’s ULE in the official directory; the local guidance for Chiclayo applies only to that district.

**If you live in Chiclayo district**

The OFIS directory lists San José 1394, at the corner of av. Quiñones, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 15:00. The report shows an update of 06-11-2026 and was consulted on 10-11-2026. Service was not confirmed by phone or visit: check the location, hours and whether an appointment is needed before travelling. Resources links to the directory.

**When submitting your application**

1. Present identity documents and the electricity bill when applicable.
2. Ask for help completing Form S100.
3. Give clear, complete and truthful information; read the consent and ask staff to explain anything you do not understand before signing.
4. Sign S100 and receive your submission receipt.
5. Keep the receipt to check your application status with the ULE.

The application is free. You do not need to pay intermediaries or bring every household member with you. If a document is missing or you have a question, ask for specific guidance.

steps.title: After the application
steps.content:
Keep your S100 submission receipt. The ULE collects the necessary information and the competent authorities assess and certify CSE; UMBRAL does not track the case.

**Information collection**

The ULE completes the Single Socioeconomic Form (FSU) at the dwelling when applicable. An adult household member can provide the information. Ask the ULE how the visit will take place and how to identify staff; the authority must resolve particular situations.

**Expected time limit**

Up to 25 working days in urban areas and 40 in rural areas, counted from the day after submitting S100. This is the time limit set by the rule, not a guarantee of observed service. If there is a delay, ask the ULE and keep your receipt.

**Status and results**

- To check your application status, ask the ULE where you submitted it.
- To check your CSE and download its certificate, use the official OFIS consultation service linked in Resources. Enter information only on the official platform.
- Having CSE does not automatically enroll you or guarantee program benefits.

**If you question the result or your situation changes**

Reassessment and updating are separate procedures with their own rules. Ask the ULE for guidance; this guide only covers a first application and does not impose a six-month wait to start one.

disclaimer.content: UMBRAL is an independent information tool; it does not represent the State or submit applications. The corresponding authorities decide classifications and benefits. Confirm local conditions before travelling. For current official information, use the links on this page.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Answers to the most common questions about Socioeconomic Classification.

items.question: What exactly is Socioeconomic Classification?
items.answer: It is a measure of household welfare used by the State. Some programs use CSE as one of their criteria, but having it does not automatically enroll you or guarantee benefits.

items.question: Does the CSE application have any cost?
items.answer: No. Applying for CSE is free and you do not need to pay intermediaries.

items.question: Can I submit my first application online?
items.answer: Official guidance for a first application says to go to the ULE of the municipality of the district where the household currently lives. Staff help you complete and sign S100 and give you a submission receipt. Check local service conditions before travelling.

items.question: How long does the process take?
items.answer: The expected time limit is up to 25 working days in urban areas and 40 in rural areas, from the day after submitting S100. This is not a guarantee of observed service. If there is a delay, ask the ULE and keep your receipt.

items.question: What if a document is missing or my DNI shows another address?
items.answer: Ask the ULE for guidance without waiting to check every box. DNI, CE, CPP and other identification recognized by the competent authority are covered. Someone temporarily lacking a document does not automatically exclude the whole household. A different DNI address alone does not require updating it before applying.

items.question: Can I apply if I rent or do not have electricity?
items.answer: Yes. You do not need to own the dwelling or be the head of the family: an adult household member can apply. An electricity bill no more than three months old is only presented if the dwelling has that service. A water bill is not a substitute general requirement.

items.question: What if I disagree with my classification?
items.answer: Ask the ULE for guidance. Reassessment and updating have their own rules and are not handled by UMBRAL. This guide only prepares a first application and does not impose a six-month wait to start one.

items.question: How do I check my application and classification?
items.answer: For your application status, ask the ULE and keep the S100 receipt. To check CSE and download its certificate, use the official OFIS service linked in Resources. Enter identity information only on that official platform; UMBRAL does not ask for it.

items.question: Is the classification permanent?
items.answer: CSE has a validity period that you should check on the official certificate. If your conditions change or validity is about to end, ask the ULE which procedure applies.

items.question: Does UMBRAL submit the application for me?
items.answer: No. UMBRAL helps prepare your first application and only saves your preparation progress on this device. It does not receive documents, submit applications, calculate CSE or decide benefits.
